pages.text: How to Save the World’s Largest Lemurs? Listen to Their Songs. | National Geographic ANIMALS How to Save the World’s Largest Lemurs? Listen to Their Songs. Scientists are employing AI-guided bioacoustics monitoring to discover how many critically endangered indri still exist in Madagascar's forests. A male indri sings in Madagascar. These endangered lemurs have complex vocals that help them claim territory in the forest. Photographs by Filippo Carugati By Sruthi Gurudev Published October 22, 2026 The tropical rainforests of Madagascar are a raucous wash of sound, pierced by astonishingly loud, musical singing. These are the vocalizations of the indri , the largest species of lemur in the world. Emanating from up in the green-black canopy, the indri songs are notably mournful and resonant—partly whale song and partly wolf howl. They rise to a crescendo and then fall away into silence. For roughly 88 million years, Madagascar has been geographically isolated from Africa and Asia. Considered something of an “ evolutionary sandbox ,” the ancestors of many of its terrestrial mammals are thought to have reached the island from continental Africa, some floating on mats of vegetation carried by ancient ocean currents. Once there, isolated populations proliferated and diversified, producing unique wildlife found nowhere else on Earth. The indri is one such animal. Endemic to the island, the species is critically endangered ; they’re threatened by habitat loss caused in part by tavy , the slash-and-burn agriculture that destroys their arboreal habitat. pages.text: How to see the Northern Lights in Canada's Edmonton region | National Geographic PAID CONTENT FOR EXPLORE EDMONTON TRAVEL How to see the Northern Lights in Canada's Edmonton region This year’s high solar activity means it’s a prime time to catch the Aurora Borealis — here’s how to spot this celestial phenomenon in and around the Alberta capital. Thanks to its northern latitude and clear night skies, Edmonton is a prime spot to view the auroras. Explore Edmonton By Brendan Sainsbury Published May 12, 2026 Nature’s most spectacular light show, the Aurora Borealis, will be even more dazzling this year. This is thanks to a phenomenon called the ‘solar maximum’, defined as the ‘peak’ of the sun’s activity over its 11-year cycle. One of the best places to take advantage of this astronomical event is in Edmonton — North America’s most northerly city, set at latitude of 53.5ºN. With a landscape of wide-open plains, Edmonton and the surrounding region offers a front-row seat to the wonders of the galaxy. Here’s how to spot the auroras using Alberta’s capital as your base. When should I go? Though the solar maximum technically occurred in 2024, this high period of solar activity is expected to continue well into 2026. Put simply, this means that the sun will be sending more electrically charged particles to Earth than usual. These then convert to green, red, purple and blue light when they collide with our atmosphere, which we see as the auroras. pages.description: Home to seals, rare birdlife and some of Britain’s best seafood restaurants, this part of East Anglia offers a peaceful break, with a coastal landscape of sand dunes and salt marshes.
pages.text: How to spend a weekend in North Norfolk, UK | National Geographic National Geographic Traveller (UK) content straight to your inbox — sign up for our newsletter here By Karlina Valeiko Published September 19, 2023 • 13 min read This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller UK. Drawing visitors since the 1700s, North Norfolk has long been a place of escapism. You arrive ready to fill your lungs with sea air and let your gaze drift to the horizon. The natural beauty here is not the kind that smacks you in the face and overwhelms with superlatives. The expansive beaches, endless skies, fenland and watery network of the Broads are a more subtle tonic for the soul — you don’t have to work too hard to forget life beyond this somewhat overlooked patch of East Anglia. It’s also a place to get closer to wildlife. Many of the salt marshes in Norfolk offer some of Britain’s best birdwatching, while seals love to sunbathe on the shingle spits at Blakeney Point. Plus, there’s bluebell and snowbell carpets in spring, dragonflies buzzing over lavender fields in summer and woodland ablaze in ochre, yellow and red in autumn. Beyond the pull of its natural attractions, North Norfolk is dotted with stately homes, sliced through by heritage railways and framed by historic towns. Add it all together and you have a region that promises the kind of serenity many search far and wide for, yet few expect to find so close to home. The resplendent quetzal is considered one of the most beautiful birds in the world. The males can grow tail feathers that are up to a metre in length. Ondrej Prosicky, Getty Images By Lorna Parkes Published May 4, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). There’s an Aztec king’s headdress — the last of its kind — in the collection of Vienna’s Weltmuseum Wien, made with nearly 400 iridescent emerald tail feathers from the quetzal bird, which have been stitched into a half-moon fan. So rare are the feathers and so vivid — despite being more than 500 years old — that the artefact, reputedly from Mexico, is reportedly worth $50m (£38m). pages.text: How to Spot the ‘Loneliest Star’ in the Autumn Night Sky | National Geographic SCIENCE NIGHT SKY GUIDE How to Spot the ‘Loneliest Star’ in the Autumn Night Sky Just 25 light-years from Earth, Fomalhaut is surrounded by vast belts of dust that could reveal the gravitational fingerprints of undiscovered worlds. Fomalhaut, one of the brightest stars in the autumn night sky, lies about 25 light-years from Earth. Roughly 15 times as luminous as our sun, the star is surrounded by vast belts of dust that may hold clues to planets astronomers have yet to discover. NASA, ESA, and the Digitized Sky Survey 2 By Stefanie Waldek Published October 23, 2026 On an autumn night in the Northern Hemisphere, Fomalhaut appears as a bright pinprick in a field of darkness, far from other bright stars. But the star’s apparent solitude is only part of its story: It sits at the center of an expansive system of dusty belts that may hold clues to worlds we have yet to find. Fomalhaut’s name comes from the Arabic fam al-ḥūt , meaning “mouth of the fish,” reflecting its place in the constellation Piscis Austrinus, or the Southern Fish. The ornithologist has shot images of birds of paradise in New Guinea, followed hornbills across Southeast Asia, and snapped pictures of cranes in Japan. April 24, 2024 How to Treat Chickenpox Key points The best way to prevent chickenpox is to get the chickenpox vaccine. Know when to call a healthcare provider if you have been exposed to chickenpox or shingles. There are steps you can take at home to help relieve chickenpox symptoms and prevent skin infections. Treatment options Over-the-counter medications Do NOT use aspirin in children with chickenpox The use of aspirin in children with chickenpox is associated with Reye's syndrome, a severe disease that affects the liver and brain and can cause death. If your child has chickenpox, use non-aspirin medications, such as acetaminophen, to help ease fever from chickenpox. You can try some simple forms of it in a meeting, on a flight or while reading this article. It can be easy to spend an entire day sitting. First at your desk at work, then perhaps in your car, followed by a couple of hours on the sofa. Before you know it, you're having dinner and realise you haven't exercised all day. Many global studies have found that a sedentary lifestyle can increase the risk of serious health conditions . Everything we can do to decrease sedentary time therefore benefits our overall health. But it can be challenging to find the time. That's where incidental exercise comes in. This is the moving around we do outside of deliberate exercise. It's also known as "non-exercise activity thermogenesis", or NEAT. This refers to any energy we use for movement that isn't sleeping, eating or deliberate exercise, says Anantha Narayanan, a research fellow at the Auckland University of Technology in New Zealand. Help for Survey Participants How We Conduct Our Surveys In addition to conducting the decennial census count, the Census Bureau conducts various surveys that study households, businesses, schools, hospitals, and more. The Census Bureau will notify you in advance if you are in a survey, provide different ways to respond, and may follow up with you. We notify you if you are in a survey. The U.S. Census Bureau typically sends an official letter describing the survey for which your household or business has been selected and why your participation is important. This letter describes what the survey is, what type of questions will be asked, and what you can expect as a survey participant. For household surveys, most mailings from the Census Bureau are addressed to “the resident of.” Household surveys from the Census Bureau are only mailed to residential addresses, not to P.O. Boxes. P.O. Boxes are not associated with specific addresses, so the Census Bureau cannot use them as a mailing destination. If you are visited by a field representative working on a survey and have not yet received a survey letter or notice from the Census Bureau, you can request one from the representative at your door. You may also contact the Census Bureau Regional Office for your state for more information. Some surveys send invitations via text message or email. You can verify an email or text message is from the Census Bureau by noting the email address or phone number from which the invitation was sent.

We have a strong history of ensuring opportunities for commercial, recreational and conservation activities on public lands under the Federal Land Policy and Management Act (FLPMA) . While resale sites are growing in popularity, in the UK we still bin about 711,000 tonnes of textiles annually – roughly the weight of seven US aircraft carriers . The global fashion and textiles industry is one of the most wasteful, but recycling firms in Peterborough and Northamptonshire are using technology to change that. They are gaining the attention of major brands but say they need laws, as well as consumers, to support them. New EU legislation requires fashion brands on sale there to demonstrate the sustainability of their products In a warehouse next to the A14 in Kettering, a mountain of crumpled fabric is slowly fed into a machine. There are dressing gowns, duvets, branded banners and lanyards from events including the Commonwealth Games. pages.text: How you can still explore the ancient city of Troy | National Geographic TRAVEL How you can still explore the ancient city of Troy Travel back in time to Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey through an ongoing excavation of the site believed to be the legendary city. A facsimile of the Trojan Horse in the port city of Çanakkale, Türkiye, draws travelers and fans of the epic Greek poems. dinosmichail, Alamy By Nick Hilden Published July 17, 2026 Driving south out of the petite port town of Çanakkale, on the northwestern tip of Türkiye, signs for “Truva” and “Troya” begin to appear with growing frequency. The bustle of modern life gives way to the pastoral, and half an hour later, you’re in the ancient city of Troy, some 3,000 years in the past. A towering wooden horse greets you at the gate and all around are scattered ruins, the Aegean Sea in the distance, and the plains upon which the legendary Trojan War was fought in between. “The aura is so strong, [that] when Caesar visited Troy he said, ‘Every stone has a name,’” says Rüstem Aslan , a professor at Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University , who has spent 40 years excavating the UNESCO World Heritage site believed to be the legendary city. Today, Hisarlik—Turkish for “ place of fortresses ,” the name for the hill where the ruins lie—recounts its history through the Troy Museum and the remains of architectural structures containing the echoes of Homer ’s great epic, The Odyssey . August 20, 2024 HPV Vaccination Key points Protect your child from certain cancers later in life with HPV vaccine. CDC recommends 2 doses of HPV vaccine at ages 11–12 years. HPV vaccination can be started at age 9 years. Introduction HPV vaccination provides safe, effective, and lasting protection against the HPV infections that most commonly cause cancer. The HPV vaccine series is most effective when given before a person is exposed to the virus. Every year in the United States, HPV causes about 36,000 cases of cancer in both men and women. But after four years in the UK, the draw of home has proven too strong and they have returned to Ukraine's third largest city, undeterred by the sustained threat of air raids. "Friends of ours thought we were idiots for going back to Ukraine," reflects John, 74. "But returning is something we felt we needed to do. "Yes, it's dangerous. Yes, there are drones flying overhead. Yes, you can hear the explosions. But you just have to get on with life as best you can. "Home is Ukraine." During their time away, the pair sought sanctuary in Hull , East Yorkshire, where John was born and raised and has a property. Human factors analysis can be used to advance our understanding of the true nature of errors in complex work settings. Research in this area has identified factors that contribute to inefficiencies and quantified the effects of human and organizational factors on performance of critical tasks. The forensic science community can benefit from the application of the substantial body of human factors work to reduce the likelihood and consequences of human error in the scientific interpretation of evidence. To assist the forensic community in this effort, the National Institute of Justice (NIJ) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s Special Programs Office partnered to develop a series of expert panels to examine human factors in forensic analyses and develop practices to reduce the likelihood of error based on scientific research. pages.text: Human jaws are surprisingly strong and efficient | National Geographic SCIENCE NOT EXACTLY ROCKET SCIENCE Human jaws are surprisingly strong and efficient By Ed Yong Published June 22, 2010 • 4 min read Stephen Wroe has built a career out of analysing some of the planet’s most formidable skulls. His group at the University of New South Wales have studied the strength, sturdiness and biting power of the sabre-toothed cat , the great white shark , and the Komodo dragon . Now, he has turned his attention to a predator whose skull is far less impressive but yields surprises all the same – us. Humans, it is said, have relatively weak jaws that can’t inflict or withstand high bite forces. Some have suggested that we are adapted to eat foods that aren’t very tough, or that our use of tools and cooking has lessened the evolutionary pressure on maintaining sturdy jaws. Some have even suggested that our weedy jaw muscles made way for our large brains and thus facilitated their evolution. But according to Wroe, all of these explanations have a fatal flaw – our jaws aren’t weak at all. They’re actually remarkably efficient for a primate. The notion of weak human chops was based on very unrefined models that treated our jaws as two-dimensional levers. Of course, in real life, we chew in three glorious dimensions. To really understand how strong our mandibles are, we need to add that third dimension to the models. That’s exactly what Wroe did. He used his signature technique, called finite element analysis , to create a virtual model of a human skull (belonging to a San hunter-gatherer).

pages.text: Humans used to have straighter teeth—what changed? | National Geographic HEALTH Humans used to have straighter teeth—what changed? New research explores how diet, evolution, and facial anatomy may have shaped our modern smiles. Studies of ancient skulls show wider jaws and fewer malocclusions, leading researchers to explore how diet and lifestyle shaped the human face. Photograph by Alan/Adobe Stock By Leah Worthington Published July 15, 2025 Braces, rubber bands, even jaw surgery—millions endure them in pursuit of a straighter smile. But were misaligned smiles always this common? Research suggests that might not be the case. While malocclusions—crowded or misaligned teeth—have been found among our hunter-gatherer ancestors, they appear to be more prevalent in modern populations. So what changed? Experts say the answer isn’t simple but point to one possible culprit: our diets. As we traded raw, tough foods for softer, more processed ones, the burden of chewing decreased, allowing our jaws to shrink over time. Now, researchers are exploring how evolutionary biology, diet, and modern lifestyles may have reshaped our faces—and our smiles. How farming may have reshaped the human face Ancient human skulls were strikingly different from our own. Early hunter-gatherers had large, powerful jaws built for the demanding work of chewing tough meats, fibrous vegetables, seeds, and nuts. But around 12,000 years ago, things began to change. pages.text: Hundreds still homeless after 'unsafe' Canning Town flats evacuation Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Hundreds still homeless after being evacuated from 'unsafe' flats 4 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ayshea Buksh London BBC The Royal Gateway, also known as Caxton Works, was advertised as "an exciting regeneration project" when it was built Hundreds of residents in east London remain homeless after structural defects were discovered at an award-winning high-rise development that was declared "at risk of sudden collapse". The Royal Gateway, also known as Caxton Works in Canning Town, Newham, was built less than 10 years ago. But last month, people living there were suddenly told to leave - some in the middle of the night by London Fire Brigade - because it was "unsafe". Businesses renting commercial spaces were also told to evacuate their premises. Engineers identified concerns with reinforced concrete "transfer slabs" supporting the buildings - an issue that has emerged at other London developments, prompting wider scrutiny of the construction method. Property company Galliard Homes, which built the scheme, says it is working to "investigate the concerns and develop potential solutions", while giving financial and practical support to residents. pages.text: Hungary v Northern Ireland: We want to play on the biggest stages - Isaac Price - BBC Sport Image source, Press Eye Image caption, West Brom midfielder Isaac Price has started Northern Ireland's last 25 matches By Andy Gray BBC Sport NI Journalist Published 16 November 2026 When Northern Ireland step out into the Puskas Arena on Tuesday night, they hope it will be a taste of what is to come. In the 70,000-seater stadium, which hosted the Champions League final between Paris St-Germain and Arsenal in May, Northern Ireland's destiny will be in their own hands. In 18 months' time, Michael O'Neill's young side will hope be at the Euro 2028 finals. But for now, they face Hungary with hopes of promotion to League A in the Nations League for the first time. A win or a draw will do the job in Budapest, and it would be the latest step for a Northern Ireland side who continue to show encouraging signs in their development. Worst case, NI will still have a shot at a play-off for League A in March but their sole aim is to get the job done on Tuesday. Midfielder Isaac Price, who has grown into a key player under O'Neill, says you "have got to love the expectation". "That's what you play football for. We're playing in a stadium where 70,000 people will be watching and then there'll be loads more at home watching," he told BBC Sport NI. "That's what you grow up and want to do. Hunting Hunting Image Details Hunting is available at more than 400 units of the National Wildlife Refuge System (national wildlife refuges and wetland management districts) and almost 20 national fish hatcheries. Hunting can be a habitat management tool to keep wildlife populations in check. Hunters' purchase of Duck Stamps helps buy conservation lands and is one of several ways hunters support conservation. All hunters must possess valid state hunting licenses. Be sure to also check regulations for each state and FWS location when planning your hunt. Related Stories Why Hunting Is Allowed on Refuges Hunting is deeply rooted in America’s heritage, and it can be an important wildlife management tool. Hydraulic Properties The Office of Geothermal’s Innovative Methods to Control Hydraulic Properties of Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) , or Hydraulic Properties, initiative supports the research, development, demonstration, and deployment of technologies and techniques to control the fluid flow within the fracture network in EGS reservoirs in order to optimize them for heat extraction. EGS systems use human-made reservoirs to access subsurface heat where natural subsurface conditions lack sufficient fluid flow—or permeability—or water to allow heat to be drawn to the surface for energy. Projects under this initiative are developing targeted and reversible in-reservoir fracture permeability modification systems or methods and yield long-term reservoir productivity improvements. The ability to customize reservoirs via these methods will increase reservoir efficiency and longevity, ultimately helping to drive down EGS costs, reduce the risk of development, and accelerate the path towards widespread commercialization. Hydrothermal Resources What Are Hydrothermal Resources? The natural formation of a hydrothermal resource requires three principal elements: heat, water, and permeability. When water is heated in the earth, hot water or steam is trapped in porous and fractured rocks beneath a layer of relatively impermeable caprock, resulting in the formation of a hydrothermal reservoir. If the conditions underground are right, humans can harness that geothermal hot water or steam by drilling and then bring it to the surface to generate electricity . These types of geothermal systems typically occur close to tectonic plate boundaries, like in the western portions of the United States. Sometimes the resource is easy to find because of indicators on the surface like hot springs. Other times, conventional geothermal resources are “ hidden ,” with no signs of the underground reservoir on the surface. Hydrothermal resources are considered conventional geothermal resources because they can be developed using existing technologies and do not require creation of human-made reservoirs as needed with enhanced geothermal systems .
